subject: Discovery follow-up: model fit, evals, and quality regression next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Bill Harper <bill.harper@acme-retail.com>, Sarita Menon <smenon@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T15:32:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps - model fit + evals

Hi Bill and Sarita,

Thanks for a productive call today - good to hear more about Acme Retail's use cases for summarization and product tagging across short and long-form content. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Key requirements: low-latency multi-document summarization for storefront pages, high precision on product attribute extraction, and consistent outputs across releases.
- Suggested model candidates: redwood/bison-2.1 (good latency/cost balance), open/gptj-13B-quant (higher throughput after quantization); I'll attach the prompt set we discussed and a short benchmark we ran on similar retail prompts.
- Next steps:
  1) I\u2019ll share the prompt set + benchmark links (attached).
  2) If you can, please send 5-10 representative documents we should add to the eval set.
  3) We\u2019ll run a focused quality eval (ranking + human review) and come back with model recommendations and a plan for staging.

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.json, acme_eval_results_20270422.csv (initial bench). Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-benchmarks

Thanks - talk soon.

-
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com

From: Bill Harper <bill.harper@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Sarita Menon <smenon@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2027-04-23T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps - model fit + evals

Marissa -

Appreciate the recap and the prompt set. Quick note: we pushed an internal update to v2.2.0 of the model last week and have seen a spike in low-confidence extractions on a subset of product pages (examples below). Is it possible that the change explains the diffs we're seeing on our side?

Examples (short):
- SKU 9921: previously returned "color": "navy" - now blank.
- Description summarization: increased hallucination in the second paragraph for long descriptions.

We\u2019re happy to share more examples but wanted to flag this as a potential quality regression - it\u2019s material for our rollout timing. Can your team look into whether the v2.2.0 change could cause this behavior?

Thanks,
Bill
VP, Product
Acme Retail

Bill - thanks for flagging, and totally hear the concern. Looping in Dev (engineering) and Ethan (product) to triage.

Dev / Ethan - Acme reported a regression after moving to v2.2.0 last week. I\u2019ve attached the initial eval CSV and the prompt set they used. They called out missing attribute extraction and more frequent hallucination on longer descriptions. Can you confirm whether any model changes in v2.2.0 could plausibly cause those diffs, and if there\u2019s a safe pin/rollback we can propose?

Proposed next steps:
- Engineering: quick triage and short diff between v2.1.0 and v2.2.0 (client-facing summary).
- If confirmed, propose a pin to v2.1.0 for Acme's production traffic and a canary rollback plan (timing + runbook).
- We\u2019ll schedule a 30-min call with Bill + Sarita once we have a proposal.

Thanks all - I attached: acme_prompt_set_v1.json, acme_eval_results_20270422.csv

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-04-24T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps - model fit + evals

Thanks for the ping, Marissa and Bill - I dug into the diffs between v2.1.0 and v2.2.0. Short summary for Acme: 

- Root cause (prelim): v2.2.0 includes a tokenizer tweak and updated decoding defaults intended to reduce repetition; in our internal eval this slightly lowered conservative extraction behavior for short key-value pairs (like single-token color fields). That matches the missing "navy" example.
- Hallucination uptick: the new decoding temperature and nucleus settings in v2.2.0 increase diversity for long-context summarization, which can surface more hallucinated content in edge cases.

Recommendation:
1) Pin Acme to model v2.1.0 for production traffic immediately to restore prior extraction behavior. We can route by account id; this is a config change and a quick rollout for dedicated/hosted customers.
2) Open a canary rollback window for up to 2 hours to validate behavior on a subset of traffic, followed by a full roll-back if metrics align.
3) Create a short customer-facing summary and runbook (attached: model-diff-v2.1.0-v2.2.0.txt and rollback-runbook.pdf).

I\u2019ve opened JIRA SUP-1234 to track the rollback work and will coordinate the infra steps. If you want, we can schedule the canary this week - earliest slot I have is Tue 2027-04-26 09:00 PDT.

-
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Inference
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Discovery recap & next steps - model fit + evals

Bill / Sarita -

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround. Per Dev\u2019s analysis, here\u2019s the customer-facing plan: 

1) Pin Acme to v2.1.0 for production (config change) - immediate.
2) Schedule a 2-hour canary rollback on 2027-04-26 09:00-11:00 PDT to validate. Dev will run the rollback with infra and report metrics within 30 minutes of the canary.
3) If canary shows restored extraction precision and no other regressions, proceed to full rollout revert.
4) Post-mortem and follow-up: Ethan will coordinate a deeper eval to tune decoding defaults for long-form summarization and produce a compatibility note for customers.

Requested from Acme: please confirm you\u2019re comfortable with the proposed canary window and whether we should expand the validation set beyond the provided examples. We\u2019ll also add the examples you sent into SUP-1234 so engineering has concrete signals.

Meeting link (30 min): https://meet.redwoodinference.com/mtg/abc-rollback
JIRA SUP-1234: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SUP-1234
